verses.text: The LORD sent Nathan to David. Nathan came to him and said, "There were two men in a certain town. One was rich, and the other was poor.
The rich man had a great many sheep and cattle.

But the poor man had nothing except one little female lamb that he had bought and raised. It grew up with him and his children. It ate from his plate, drank from his cup, and slept in his arms. It was like a daughter to him.

One day a traveller came to visit the rich man. The rich man did not want to take one of his own sheep or cattle to cook for his visitor. Instead, he took the poor man's lamb and cooked it for the man who had come to him."
David became very angry with the rich man. He said to Nathan, "As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
He must pay back four lambs for that one, because he did such a thing and had no pity!"
Then Nathan said to David, "You are that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from Saul.
I gave you your master's palace and put your master's wives into your arms. I gave you the people of Israel and Judah. And if that had been too little, I would have given you much more.

So why have you treated the LORD's word with contempt by doing what is evil in his eyes? You killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife to be your wife. You had him killed by the sword of the Ammonites.
So now the sword will never leave your family, because you treated me with contempt and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own wife.'

This is what the LORD says: 'I am going to bring trouble on you from your own family. Right in front of your eyes I will take your wives and give them to someone close to you, and he will sleep with your wives in broad daylight.
You did your sin in secret, but I will do this openly in front of all Israel, in the light of day.'"
Then David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." Nathan answered David, "The LORD has taken away your sin. You will not die.
But because what you did has given the LORD's enemies a reason to speak against him, the son born to you will die."
Then Nathan went home. The LORD struck the child that Uriah's widow had borne to David, and the child became very sick.
David begged God for the child. He went without food, and he went in and spent the nights lying on the ground.
The older leaders of his household stood beside him and tried to get him up from the ground, but he refused, and he would not eat any food with them.

On the seventh day the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead. They said, "While the child was still alive, we spoke to David, but he would not listen to us. How can we tell him the child is dead? He may do something to hurt himself."
But David noticed that his servants were whispering to each other, and he understood that the child was dead. He asked his servants, "Is the child dead?" They answered, "Yes, he is dead."

Then David got up from the ground. He washed, put on lotion, and changed his clothes. He went into the house of the LORD and worshipped. Then he went home and asked for food, and they served him, and he ate.
His servants said to him, "Why are you acting like this? While the child was alive, you fasted and cried for him. But now that the child is dead, you get up and eat!"
David answered, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and cried. I thought, 'Who knows? Maybe the LORD will be kind to me and let the child live.'
But now he is dead. Why should I go without food? Can I bring him back again? One day I will go to him, but he will not come back to me."
Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba. He slept with her, and she had a son, and David named him Solomon. The LORD loved the child,
and he sent word through Nathan the prophet that the baby should be named Jedidiah, which means loved by the LORD, because the LORD loved him.
Meanwhile, Joab was fighting against Rabbah, the Ammonite capital, and he captured the royal fortress.
Joab sent messengers to David to say, "I have fought against Rabbah and captured its water supply.
Now bring the rest of the army together, surround the city, and capture it. Otherwise I will capture it, and it will be named after me."
So David gathered the whole army, went to Rabbah, attacked it, and captured it.

He took the crown off their king's head and put it on his own head. It was made of gold, about thirty-four kilograms, and it had precious stones in it. David also carried away a great amount of goods from the city.

He brought out the people who lived there and made them work with saws, iron picks, and iron axes, and made them work at making bricks. He did this to all the Ammonite towns. Then David and his whole army went back to Jerusalem.
